claims.subject: MCP surface: `watch` and `init` tools
claims.why: The original asks for a complete MCP surface, but TOOLS and dispatch expose only 8 of the 10 CLI commands; there is no `watch` or `init`, so a Bot that rents through MCP cannot start the guard that enforces the cap (docs/mcp.md says the same).

claims.subject: guard idle rule (guard.watch / Snapshot.effective_idle_minutes)
claims.why: watch() passes wall-clock time since the guard started as `idle_since_start_minutes` whatever the GPU utilisation, and effective_idle_minutes takes the max, so any watched pod, even a busy one, is stopped as 'idle' once idle_minutes have passed; docs/cap.md describes the rule as 'GPU utilisation held at 0 for the idle window', and no test covers watch with a non-zero interval.

claims.subject: MCP `rentguard_run` command handling
claims.why: dispatch splits the command string on whitespace and cli._remote_command then shell-quotes each word, so a compound command sent over MCP (e.g. 'mkdir -p results; hostname > x') reaches the remote shell as quoted words; that is the M2 defect the CLI fixed, so MCP `run` no longer means what CLI `run` means.

claims.subject: documentation of F-4 (--dry-run) and F-5 (idle clamp)
claims.why: KNOWN-FAILURES, cap.md, quickstart.md, limitations.md and VERIFICATION.md all say `up --dry-run` rents a machine ('do not use') and that the idle reading is unclamped with no test, but cli.py checks dry_run before any create, guard._idle_minutes_since_boot clamps to uptime, and tests/test_money_paths.py covers both, so the documentation the original asked for now describes behaviour the code does not have.

claims.subject: documented test counts and status wording
claims.why: The docs give 74 tests with test_money_paths.py at 33, but that file now has about 39 and tests/test_runpod_transport.py is not listed at all; the documented guard lines ('NO HEARTBEAT — nothing is watching this instance', 'heartbeat 12.4 min old — the guard is probably dead') also differ from what cli.cmd_status prints ('NO GUARD — …', 'probably dead (heartbeat … min old)').

claims.subject: KNOWN-FAILURES F-1 and F-3 still listed as open
claims.why: The file's own rule removes a defect once a test covers it, yet F-1 is covered by tests/test_known_failures.py and tests/test_drift.py, and F-3's required instance stamping exists as cli._instance_name with tests in test_money_paths.py, and both are still presented as open defects.

claims.subject: end-to-end proof of the guard (`watch`) on a real rented GPU
claims.why: The original asks for an end-to-end proof on a real rented GPU, but VERIFICATION.md says `watch` stopping a live pod was 'never through the CLI against a real machine', and the M2 runs (docs/M2-REAL-RENTAL.md) cover up/run/pull/down only, at a revision before the dry-run, idle-clamp and two-sample fixes.

claims.subject: record of the real-GPU proof (count and cost)
claims.why: CHANGELOG.md, docs/M2-REAL-RENTAL.md and docs/quickstart.md record two rentals for $0.017, while CHARTER.md R5 records 3 rentals for $0.0264, and CHARTER W4 says a paid run's guard stopped a 32-second-old pod, which VERIFICATION.md says never happened through the CLI, so the evidence for the original's e2e requirement contradicts itself.

claims.subject: tests/_artefacts/ (probe scripts and assay run logs)
claims.why: Internal audit transcripts (UTF-16 PowerShell captures with German error noise, 'NO GIT COMMIT' run logs) and one-off probe scripts that write to .assay-tmp ship in the tree of what the original asked to be a publishable release, and nothing asked for them.

claims.subject: 94% line coverage / 100% feature coverage target and CI ratchet
claims.why: The original asks to harden the money-critical paths with tests; the numeric 94%/100% target (CHARTER R10, the CI comment 'the target the user set') does not appear in the original and may come from conversation the frozen text does not record.
